c.tagline: New Zealand's sunniest city and craft-loving gateway to Abel Tasman.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis such as Nelson City Taxis and Sun City Taxis are the main option; Uber coverage is very limited, so booking a local cab by phone or app is more reliable.

emergency.note: 111 is the single emergency number for police, fire and ambulance across New Zealand; Nelson Hospital runs the region's main emergency department.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_desc: The compact heart of Nelson around Trafalgar Street and the hilltop Christ Church Cathedral, packed with cafes, galleries, boutiques and the Saturday market; the most walkable base for first-timers.
A leafy heritage neighbourhood of restored villas just north of the centre, within walking distance of town yet quiet and residential; suits travellers wanting character and calm.
Nelson's main beach suburb on a long golden sweep of sand with a holiday park, playground and cafes; a relaxed, family-friendly base a short drive or bus ride from town.
The waterfront strip along Wakefield Quay and Port Nelson, lined with seafood restaurants and bars looking over the harbour and Tasman Bay; best for dining and sunset views.
A larger suburban area between Nelson and Richmond with shopping, Founders Heritage Park nearby and easy access to wineries; a practical, budget-friendly base with more space.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink.

transit.hours: NBus services run roughly 7am to 7pm on weekdays with limited Saturday services and little or no Sunday or evening service; taxis fill the gaps outside those hours.
transit.note: Nelson's public transport is the small NBus network run by Nelson City Council; there is no rail, and the flat, compact centre is easily walked or cycled.
transit.pay: Tap on and off with a prepaid Bee Card for the cheapest fare, or pay the driver with cash; the network is limited, so many visitors rely on walking, cycling or taxis.

bus: InterCity coaches to Picton, Blenheim, Christchurch and the West Coast
Abel Tasman shuttle services to Motueka, Kaiteriteri and Marahau
ferry: Abel Tasman water taxis from Kaiteriteri and Marahau (seasonal, ~1 hr drive from the city)

transit.m: Super Shuttle door-to-door shared van to the city (~15 min)
Airport taxi to central Nelson (~10 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in New Zealand; rounding up or leaving ~10% for exceptional service is appreciated but never expected.
